predecessors.name: Hafsids of Béjaïa
predecessors.text: the Kalaa, where Emir Abderrahmane withdrew after the Spanish took Béjaïa in 1510

successors.name: French Africa
successors.text: the Kalaa and the Medjana: 'The Kalaa itself, impregnable since the 16th century, surrendered on 22 July 1871'

ledger.x: 1559-1596 (bridge): Ahmed Amokrane extends the kingdom to the Sahara.
1849: the French detach the Hodna tribes.

wars.name: Algiers against the Kalaa
wars.outcome: The Barbarossa brothers attacked Abdelaziz near Béjaïa in 1516 and he submitted; the Regency made the Kalaa's lord its khalifa in the Medjana in 1542; he repulsed two Turkish expeditions in 1550; the Kalaa was attacked in 1552-1553; Hassan Pasha attacked it…

wars.name: Khizr Pasha's siege and Ahmed Amokrane's campaign against Algiers
wars.outcome: Khizr Pasha besieged the Kalaa for two months in 1590 and failed; Ahmed Amokrane paid 30,000 douros for recognition of independence; he besieged Algiers for eleven days in 1598 and was killed in 1600 after beating Soliman Veneziano.

wars.name: Battle of Guidjel
wars.outcome: On 20 September 1638 the tribes and Constantine fought the Pasha of Algiers; the victory led to independence from Algiers.

wars.name: Mokrani revolt
wars.outcome: The revolt began on 15 March 1871 (the Rahmaniyya joined on 8 April); Mohamed Mokrani died on 5 May 1871 and the Kalaa surrendered on 22 July.

certainty.note: The pages give no frontier; the Bordj Bou Arréridj and M'Sila provinces and the 40 km oasis circles are the researcher's.
